subject: religious-studies
title: AQA Evil and Religious Experience
welcome_lead: Cover two further AQA staples: theodicy and the argument from religious experience.
meta_desc: AQA A-Level Religious Studies adventure on the problem of evil and religious experience.
final_note: Suffering and encounter test classical theism in opposite directions.

concepts.def: Evil as privation, entering creation through the free-will Fall of angels and humans.
Humans as immature creations growing through suffering into the likeness of God.
Plantinga's argument that genuine free creatures necessarily make some morally bad choices.
Mystical experience is ineffable, noetic, transient, and passive (Varieties, 1902).
Non-rational experience of the holy as mysterium tremendum et fascinans (1917).
Credulity (things are as they seem unless defeaters arise) and testimony (others' reports should be trusted), used to defend religious experience.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Augustine (354-430) accounts for evil as the privation of good arising from the misuse of free will. Irenaeus (c. 130-202), developed by Hick (1966), sees humans as created immature, with evil as the context for soul-making.

Plantinga (1974) defends the logical coherence of free will against Mackie's inconsistent triad.

William James' Varieties of Religious Experience (1902) studies mysticism empirically. Rudolf Otto's The Idea of the Holy (1917) names the numinous as a unique religious category.

Richard Swinburne defends the cognitive significance of such experiences through his principles of credulity and testimony.

Critics like Bertrand Russell and J.L. Mackie argue that religious experience admits naturalistic explanation (e.g. psychological, neurological).

Defenders reply that this is to confuse mechanism with meaning: showing how an experience occurs does not show that it lacks veridical content.

mcqs.q: Whose 1917 The Idea of the Holy introduced the numinous?
Who develops the Irenaean theodicy in Evil and the God of Love (1966)?

numericals.q: In what year was William James' Varieties of Religious Experience published?

free_texts.q: What is Swinburne's principle that things are probably as they seem unless defeaters arise?
